title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Cal Lutheran rituals and recurring campus gatherings, from the ridge-top rocks to student-programmed seasonal events.

cards.title: Paint the CLU Rocks
cards.subtitle: Mount Clef Ridge overlooking campus
cards.notes: View the ridge landmark from campus; painting is reserved for the annual freshman and transfer-student tradition.
cards.short_summary: A long-running welcome ritual centered on the giant CLU letters above campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran says the CLU rocks have been a fixture since 1962 and that freshman and transfer students paint them every year.
cards.access_notes: Observe from permitted campus areas; the official page identifies painting as an annual freshman and transfer-student activity.

cards.title: Learn the Violet and Gold Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: Cal Lutheran’s school song, written in 1961
cards.notes: Read the official lyrics before a campus ceremony or reunion, and listen for the repeated violet-and-gold refrain.
cards.short_summary: The school song names Cal Lutheran, its surrounding hills, and its violet-and-gold colors.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s official glossary identifies its Alma Mater, credits Orville Dahl and Rossini/Ramsey, and dates it to 1961.
cards.access_notes: Lyrics are publicly available on the official glossary page.

cards.title: Return for the Scandinavian Festival
cards.subtitle: Annual Nordic-heritage gathering on the Cal Lutheran campus
cards.notes: Check the festival’s official schedule before going; the university describes music, dance, crafts, storytelling, and heritage activities.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus festival connecting Cal Lutheran’s Scandinavian roots with Nordic cultural programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran describes the Scandinavian Festival as an annual event celebrating the university’s Scandinavian heritage.
cards.access_notes: Confirm dates, admission, and activities with the festival’s current official information before attending.

cards.title: Mark the ASCLUG Fall Carnival
cards.subtitle: Kingsmen Park
cards.notes: Use the ASCLUG calendar for the current date and plan to arrive during the listed event window at Kingsmen Park.
cards.short_summary: A student-government fall gathering built around carnival games and live entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: ASCLUG lists its Fall Carnival at Kingsmen Park as a fall-semester event with carnival games and live entertainment.
cards.access_notes: The current ASCLUG calendar lists the 2026 event for October 16, 6–10 p.m.; verify future dates before attending.

cards.title: Catch Let It Snow
cards.subtitle: End-of-semester event at Kingsmen Park
cards.notes: Look to ASCLUG’s event calendar near semester’s end and use the posted time and location for the current edition.
cards.short_summary: ASCLUG’s seasonal campus celebration brings holiday programming to Kingsmen Park.
cards.evidence_claim: ASCLUG’s official events page lists Let It Snow as an end-of-semester celebration at Kingsmen Park.
cards.access_notes: The current ASCLUG calendar lists the 2026 event for December 4, 6–8 p.m.; verify future dates before attending.

cards.title: Follow Competing for the Crown
cards.subtitle: ASCLUG Programs Board event
cards.notes: Check the student-events calendar for the current format and timing; this is one of the Programs Board’s named campus events.
cards.short_summary: A named ASCLUG Programs Board gathering listed alongside Fall Carnival and Let It Snow.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s catalog names Competing for the Crown as an ASCLUG Programs Board-sponsored student event.
cards.source_title: Student Life — California Lutheran University Catalog
cards.access_notes: No current date or format was verified; consult ASCLUG’s current events calendar.

cards.title: Say Buh Bye to the Semester
cards.subtitle: ASCLUG end-of-semester gathering
cards.notes: Watch the student-events calendar late in spring and follow the official listing for the current venue and activity details.
cards.short_summary: A named Cal Lutheran send-off event for the end of the academic semester.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s student-life catalog identifies Buh Bye Bash among events sponsored by the Office of Student Life.
cards.source_title: Student Life — California Lutheran University Catalog
cards.access_notes: A 2026 listing placed Buh Bye Bash at Samuelson Aquatics Center; verify the current event listing before attending.

cards.entity_name: Raíces y Ritmos: Latine Heritage Fiesta
cards.title: Join Raíces y Ritmos
cards.subtitle: Annual Latine Heritage Fiesta at Kingsmen Park
cards.notes: Check the calendar around Latine Heritage Month and use the current listing for program details and attendance information.
cards.short_summary: A sixth-annual campus fiesta recognizing Latine Heritage Month through community, culture, music, and connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s events calendar calls Raíces y Ritmos its sixth annual Latine Heritage Fiesta and says it honors Latine Heritage Month.
cards.source_title: The Hub — Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, Justice and Belonging
cards.access_notes: The current calendar lists a September 25, 2026 event at Kingsmen Park; verify future dates before attending.

cards.title: See Dragged Out
cards.subtitle: CCEI’s annual celebration of the art of drag
cards.notes: Consult the CCEI calendar for the current date, venue, and participation details before making plans for this performance event.
cards.short_summary: An annual CCEI event celebrating drag performance and self-expression on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s events calendar describes Dragged Out as the CCEI’s annual celebration of the art of drag.
cards.access_notes: The current calendar lists a 2026 event at Lundring Events Center; verify future dates and access information before attending.

cards.title: Trace the Choir’s Annual Tour
cards.subtitle: A tradition first recorded in 1962
cards.notes: Look for current choir announcements or concert listings; the university history records the first annual tour with 50 student singers.
cards.short_summary: A music tradition whose first annual tour is documented in Cal Lutheran’s institutional history.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s history states that its Choir began its first annual tour in April 1962 with 50 students.
cards.access_notes: The history page documents the tradition’s 1962 beginning; no current tour schedule was verified.
